transcript:
Header: 2026-11-24 15:00 PST | Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Olivia (Zephyr Head of Search), Ravi (ML Eng), Sofia (Product), Tom (Eng Manager)
Links shared: Redwood hosted API quickstart (link), rerank runbook (link), security pack (SOC2 + ISO) [Maya to send].

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:03] Olivia: yep, loud and clear!
[00:08] Maya: great — quick agenda, we'll do a 10-15m context/qualify, then a live demo of embeddings + rerank flows, console quick tour, and wrap w/ next steps. sound good?
[00:18] Ravi: sounds good. our main goal is improving relevancy for product search and cutting down on manual tuning — latency target is sub-60ms p95 for rerank, cost needs to be practical.
[00:28] Ethan: perfect, that helps. couple quick qual Qs — where are you hosting your index today? elastic or a vector store?
[00:33] Tom: we run OpenSearch for primary inverted index and a custom vector store right now, some embeddings live in a managed Pinecone test cluster.
[00:42] Maya: ok good, so hybrid stack, familiar pattern. timeline for pilot?
[00:45] Sofia: we'd like to run something in dev in December and evaluate before EOY to decide on Q1 rollout.
[00:52] Maya: cool — success criteria?
[00:54] Olivia: higher NDCG / improved click-through on top-k, and must not add >20ms median latency to current pipeline; p95 under 60ms. also security — SOC2, SSO and audit logs required.
[01:05] Ethan: noted. Redwood Hosted supports SAML SSO, audit logs and SOC2 docs — I'll drop the full pack.

[01:20] Maya: ok hopping into the demo — I'll share my screen, Ethan will drive the technical bits. [slides shared]

[01:30] Ethan: quick architecture — step 1: embed corpus/docs (we support a few models in the catalog), step 2: store vectors in your vector store (we can push to Pinecone/managed or we can host embeddings through Redwood), step 3: search candidate retrieval, step 4: rerank using Redwood rerank endpoint that takes the query, candidates (ids + embeddings) and returns reranked list.
[01:52] Ravi: wait, so rerank runs on Redwood Hosted? what about private data? is KV cache stored?
[01:57] Ethan: rerank runs on Redwood Hosted by default; for private deployments we have Dedicated or Private options. KV cache is ephemeral per request and not persisted beyond the inference lifecycle; we also support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest for Private.
[02:12] Olivia: and data retention — we cannot have raw queries retained >30 days without consent.
[02:16] Maya: understood, our hosted retention default is 30 days but we can negotiate in the SOW; for enterprise we do a Private control plane option and support custom retention policies. I'll include that in the notes.

[02:35] Ethan: demo time — I'll call the embeddings endpoint with a sample doc and show cosine similarity vectors (note: transcription may say cosign sometimes). [terminal shared]
[02:50] Ethan: sample request: POST /v1/embeddings model=text-embedding-002 input=["product description ..."] -> returns 1536-d vector. then we push vectors to Pinecone via their SDK.
[03:08] Olivia: are model choices fixed? we need a stable embedding that doesn't drift between releases.
[03:12] Ethan: you can pin model versions in Redwood, and we have model profiles showing differences; we recommend pinning for production to avoid drift during A/B.

[03:35] Ethan: next — rerank endpoint. Here's a sample payload: {query:..., candidates: [{id:1, embedding:[...]}, ...], context: {user_locale:...}} -> response is scored list with explainability scores.
[03:55] Ravi: explainability — can we get feature-level signals? like token-level attention or simple signal contributions?
[03:59] Ethan: we expose a score breakdown (embedding sim, cross-encoder score, length penalty) not raw attention weights; it's meant to be actionable. full interpretability can be limited because some models are large but we include a per-candidate score breakdown.

[04:20] [05:00] Olivia: we care about latency — can rerank be batched? our workload is many concurrent queries but short candidate lists.
[05:07] Ethan: yes, Redwood supports batching and continuous batching in the runtime; batching increases throughput but can affect latency — we can tune batch windows and SLOs. For your tight p95 target, we might recommend a small batch window and a dedicated capacity for rerank to avoid noisy neighbors.
[05:30] Tom: how much does Dedicated cost relative to Hosted? can we do hosted with reserved capacity?
[05:35] Maya: we have Dedicated (reserved GPUs) and Hosted with burstable dedicated lanes — pricing varies; I'll send an example pricing sheet. Usually Dedicated is ~X-2X higher but gives guaranteed latency and isolation.

[05:55] Ethan: switching to Console — here you can create routes, pin model versions, view token-level cost charts, and set automatic fallbacks. For rerank we show per-route latency histograms and per-model token cost. [console shown]
[06:20] Sofia: can we instrument traces to correlate user id -> route -> model?
[06:24] Ethan: yes, you can attach request IDs and the tracing hooks push to your observability. We also export per-request metadata to your logging sink.

[06:40] [07:10] Olivia: question on vector stores — we have a mix of Pinecone and OpenSearch. does Redwood require moving all vectors?
[07:16] Ethan: no — we support hybrid. you can keep your primary inverted index in OpenSearch and store embeddings where you prefer. Redwood's rerank accepts candidate embeddings inline, so you can fetch candidates from your index and call rerank w/ embeddings either supplied inline or by referencing IDs if we host vectors.
[07:34] Ravi: so minimal infra changes, good. for the rerank model size — what throughput can we expect on say a 4xA100 job?
[07:41] Ethan: rough order of magnitude: for a cross-encoder rerank model (7B-ish), you might get X qps per GPU—we included benchmark numbers in the runbook; we'll run a tailored benchmark for your candidate length and sequence lengths.

[08:05] Maya: ok demo of a rerank run — I'll show a before/after using your small dataset sample we prepared earlier. [demo query run - simulated data]
[08:20] Ethan: initial retrieval returned top-50 candidates from OpenSearch, then rerank using Redwood returned top-5 with better relevance — metrics: MRR up ~12% in this toy run. keep in mind toy data, will vary on production corpus.
[08:40] Olivia: nice — can we regularize scores to prevent stale docs surfacing?
[08:43] Ethan: yes you can include freshness features in the candidate payload and we expose those as context features to the reranker.

[09:00] [09:30] Sofia: security — can you share SOC2 and encryption details? also SSO.
[09:35] Maya: yes SOC2 Type II pack is in the security docs I'll share; we support SAML SSO, RBAC roles, audit logs, and can integrate with customer KMS on Private. For Hosted, data-in-transit is TLS, at-rest encryption is AES-256 with our managed KMS unless customer-managed KMS requested under enterprise plan.
[09:58] Ravi: any egress/residency controls? we need Europe data to remain in eu-west region.
[10:03] Ethan: region routing supported — you can route requests to eu regions and we can pin model serving to a region. Private deployments give the strongest residency controls if required.

[10:25] Tom: one more on cost — how do you measure per-rerank token cost? we want predictable unit economics.
[10:30] Ethan: Console shows per-request cost broken down: embedding compute + rerank model compute + tokenization overhead. For rerank we can provide per-1000-requests estimate based on candidate lengths. We'll include example unit economics in the pricing sheet.

[11:00] [11:40] Olivia: what's the onboarding friction — how long to get a pilot up and running?
[11:45] Maya: typical pilot can start in 1-2 weeks after legal/NDAs, data handoff and test dataset. Pilot runs ~2-4 weeks for meaningful metrics. For your timeline, starting first week of December aligns to a mid-December evaluation.
[12:05] Sofia: ok we'll aim for week of Dec 7 for kickoff as discussed.

[12:25] Ethan: small technical note — if you want to avoid moving vectors, we can accept compressed embeddings (quantized) and perform rerank on compressed representations; this reduces network egress. There's also an Optimize recommendation flow that suggests quantization profiles per model.
[12:45] Ravi: interesting — how does quantization affect accuracy?
[12:48] Ethan: small drop for some models — Optimize provides offline suggestions and we can run an A/B to measure degradation. We'll include recommended profiles in the runbook.

[13:10] Maya: ok quick recap then next steps.
[13:15] Maya: recap — Redwood Hosted API can run embeddings + rerank; you can keep your vector store or host with us; Console gives the routing, observability and cost breakdowns; Dedicated/Private available if residency/latency requires it. Agreed pilot: Zephyr to provide anonymized 5k query set, Redwood to run benchmark and share results, security docs + pricing to be sent.
[13:36] Olivia: sounds right. couple caveats — legal will want minimal data retention and plain language on logging.
[13:42] Maya: understood — action items captured.

[13:50] Tom: any blockers from Redwood side for the pilot?
[13:52] Ethan: none — we'd just need the test data and a short SSO config if you want to see Console. For the benchmark we'll need candidate lengths and typical top-k size.

[14:15] Sofia: ok we'll gather and share.

[14:20] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and proposed kickoff calendar item.
[14:26] Olivia: thanks Maya, Ethan. bye.
[14:28] Maya: thanks all. bye.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had a few mis-hearings (cosign vs cosine, pipelines vs pinwalls), speaker labels sometimes shifted mid-call.

Attachments / Links to send: pricing_deck.pdf (Maya), rerank_runbook.md (Ethan), SOC2_security_pack.zip (Maya), benchmark-notebook.ipynb (Ethan), shared S3 upload link for test dataset (to be created by Zephyr).

End of transcript.
